To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ATP-induced iodine efflux involves parallel activation of PLA2 and PLC, that PLA2 activation is not mediated by PKC or by increased cytosolic Ca, but that PLA2 activation leads to an increase in PKC activity, and that PKC activation leads to increased iodine efflux.
ATP increases inositiol phosphate and cytosolic calcium, arachidonic release and iodide efflx, and this involves parallel, not serial, activation of phospholipase-C and -A2.
extracellular ATP stimulates inositol phosphate production and calcium release in FRTL- 5 cells by activating PLC and PKC, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of ATP-induced iodide release in FRTL- 5 cells.
the mechanism of P2-purinoceptor-mediated stimulation of iodide release from the thyroid.
the role of the phosphoinositide (PI) pathway in the regulation of thyroid function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P2-purinoceptors are coupled to both PLC and PLA2, and the activation of these enzymes are not sequential, but rather parallel.
P2-purinoceptor activation of PLC and subsequent IP3 formation is required for the increase in 125-125I efflux in FRLT-5 rat thyroid follicular cells.
ATP stimulates PLC and PLA2 in FRTL- 5 cells, and that the activation of both enzymes is required for the increase in 125 I efflux.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP increases inosital phosphates, [Ca2+]I and AA release, and iodine efflux in FTRL-5 thyroid cells.
ATP-induced iodine release is mediated by a PLC- and PLA2- dependent pathway, but the increase in calcium is not necessary to mediate iodine release.

the P2-purinoceptor activation of PLC, PKC, and PLA2 in thyroid cells results in the activation of a protein kinase, which phosphorylates a protein, and this phosphorylated protein is responsible for the activation of iodide transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
P2-purinoceptor activation of PLC and PLC are not sequential, but parallel, events.
the P2 purinergic receptors are involved in a variety of cellular processes in thyroid cells.
the P2-purinoceptor is a complex signaling system that can activate multiple signaling pathways.
